mainTopic: The fast-day שליח ציבור, the twenty-four ברכות, and how the order differs inside and outside the מקדש
overview: The גמרא finishes explaining רבי יהודה's list of qualities for a fast-day שליח ציבור. It shows that 'his house is empty' means empty of sin, and it explains 'his youth was pleasant.' A פסוק in ירמיהו about a voice God hates is read as describing an unworthy חזן. Next the גמרא asks how the משנה's six added ברכות fit with its mention of a 'seventh' one. רב נחמן בר יצחק answers that the seventh counts the lengthened ברכת גואל ישראל. A ברייתא then lays out the order: each added ברכה ends with 'He Who answered...', the people respond, and the שופר calls switch between תקיעה and תרועה. Outside the מקדש the people answer אמן. In the מקדש they answer 'ברוך שם כבוד מלכותו', based on a פסוק in נחמיה. When רבי חלפתא and רבי חנניה בן תרדיון used the מקדש order in their towns, the חכמים limited it to the מקדש. Finally the גמרא begins to explain why רבי יהודה leaves out זכרונות and שופרות, and the answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Aren't two of the qualities the same thing?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי יהודה lists both 'burdened with children and has nothing' and 'his house is empty,' since they seem to mean the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't 'burdened with children and has nothing' the same as 'his house is empty'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that two items in רבי יהודה's list seem to say the same thing, so one of them looks extra.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A poor man with many children has an empty house. So listing both phrases looks repetitive. The גמרא assumes each phrase must teach something different.

keyTerms.meaning: Isn't that the same as...? (points out that two things look identical)
Burdened, loaded down with a family to support
His house is empty

phrases.english: Isn't 'burdened with children and has nothing'
phrases.notes: These words come from רבי יהודה's list, just before this, of what the חזן on a fast day should be like.

phrases.english: the same as 'his house is empty'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the explanation of רבי יהודה's list from the earlier part of the daf.
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase 'ביתו ריקם' in רבי יהודה's list
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two phrases in the list seem to mean the same thing, so one looks unnecessary.

steps.title: His house is empty of sin
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא explains that 'his house is empty' means his home is free of sin, not empty of money.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: this means his house is empty of sin.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers the question by giving 'his house is empty' a different meaning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Burdened and has nothing' is about poverty. 'His house is empty' is about how the home behaves: nothing sinful goes on in it. So the two phrases teach two separate qualities.

keyTerms.meaning: A sin, a wrongdoing

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
This is one whose house is empty of sin.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives one of the phrases a new meaning
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both phrases describe poverty, so one is extra.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'ביתו ריקם' means free of sin, so each phrase teaches something different.

steps.title: What 'his youth was pleasant' means
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that 'פרקו נאה' means the person never had a bad reputation when he was young.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And his youth was pleasant': אביי said, this is someone who never had a bad name in his youth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains another phrase in רבי יהודה's list, using אביי's words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It is not enough for the חזן to be good now. Even in his younger years, people must not have spoken badly about him. His past has to be clean too.

keyTerms.meaning: His youth (his early years) was pleasant and proper
A bad reputation
His youth, his childhood

phrases.english: 'And his youth was pleasant':
Abaye said:

phrases.aramaic: זֶה שֶׁלֹּא יָצָא עָלָיו שֵׁם רַע בְּיַלְדוּתוֹ.
phrases.english: This is one about whom no bad name went out in his youth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next phrase in the same list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A fast-day חזן must never have had a bad reputation, even in his youth.
steps.whatToRemember: The fast-day חזן must be poor and burdened (so he prays from the heart), his home must be free of sin, and his past must be clean.

steps.title: A פסוק about a voice God hates
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a פסוק from ירמיהו and asks what 'she has given her voice against me' means.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'My heritage has become to me like a lion in the forest; she gave her voice against me, therefore I hate her.' What does 'she gave her voice against me' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק and asks about one confusing phrase in it. This sets up the next step, which explains it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks of a 'voice' that God hates, and the גמרא wants to know whose voice this is. The question connects back to the topic of who should lead the prayers.

keyTerms.meaning: My heritage, my inheritance (here: the Jewish people)
She raised her voice against me
I hated her

phrases.english: 'My heritage has become to me like a lion in the forest;

phrases.aramaic: נָתְנָה עָלַי בְּקוֹלָהּ עַל כֵּן שְׂנֵאתִיהָ״,
phrases.english: she has given her voice against me; therefore I hate her.'
What is 'she has given her voice against me'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a פסוק connected to the topic of the fitting חזן.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whose 'voice' is the פסוק talking about?

steps.title: An unworthy חזן
steps.stepSummary: The 'voice' God hates is the prayer of a שליח ציבור who is not worthy to lead.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא בר טוביה said in the name of רב, and some say רבי חמא said in the name of רבי אלעזר: this is an unworthy prayer leader who goes down before the ark.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: the hated 'voice' is that of an unfit חזן leading the congregation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When an unworthy person leads the prayers, his voice does not bring God closer; it pushes Him away. This shows why the qualities listed above are so important. Two chains of names are given for who said it.

keyTerms.meaning: The prayer leader, the one who prays for the congregation
Worthy, fitting
Who 'goes down before the ark', meaning who leads the prayers

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר מָר זוּטְרָא בַּר טוֹבִיָּה אָמַר רַב,
phrases.english: Mar Zutra bar Toviyya said that Rav said,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ אָמַר רַבִּי חָמָא אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר:
phrases.english: and some say Rabbi Chama said that Rabbi Elazar said:
This is a prayer leader who is not worthy
who goes down before the ark.
phrases.notes: In the old shuls the חזן stood in a spot lower than the rest, so leading the prayers was called 'going down.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר זוּטְרָא בַּר טוֹבִיָּה אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The hated voice is that of an unworthy שליח ציבור.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for being careful about who leads the congregation in prayer, especially at a time of trouble.
steps.whatToRemember: An unworthy חזן's prayer is described as a voice God 'hates', so choosing a fitting שליח ציבור really matters.

steps.title: The משנה: twenty-four ברכות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: the fast-day חזן says twenty-four ברכות, the usual eighteen plus six more.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he says before them twenty-four blessings: the eighteen of every day, and he adds six more to them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and quotes its next line. This sets up a question about the count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On a תענית ציבור the חזן's שמונה עשרה gets longer. The משנה gives a clear total of 24: the regular 18 plus 6 extra.

keyTerms.meaning: Twenty-four blessings
The eighteen blessings of the daily עמידה
And he adds

phrases.english: And he says before them twenty-four blessings:
the eighteen of every day,
and he adds to them another six.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the חזן's qualities and goes to the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On a fast day the חזן says 24 ברכות: 18 regular and 6 added.

steps.title: Six or seven extra ברכות?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the count: a later line of the משנה speaks of a 'seventh' added ברכה, so there seem to be seven.
steps.simpleTranslation: These six are really seven! As we learned: on the seventh he says 'Blessed is He Who has mercy on the land'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the number six, because a later line of the משנה talks about a 'seventh' extra ברכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If there is a 'seventh' ברכה, then there must be seven additions, and the total would be 25, not 24. The משנה seems to contradict itself.

keyTerms.meaning: They are, they come out to
As we learned in a משנה
Seventh
Who has mercy on the land

phrases.english: These six are really seven!
As we learned in a משנה:
On the seventh he says:
'Blessed is He Who has mercy on the land'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the number given in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's count of six added ברכות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same משנה later mentions a 'seventh' added ברכה, which would mean seven additions.

steps.title: Seventh counting the lengthened ברכה
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק explains that 'seventh' counts the long, stretched-out ברכה too, so there are still only six new ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: What is 'seventh'? Seventh for the long one.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers that 'seventh' does not mean a seventh new ברכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One regular ברכה of שמונה עשרה is made much longer on a fast day. Counting that long ברכה along with the new ones, the last one comes out 'seventh', but only six are truly new. So the total stays at 24.

keyTerms.meaning: For the long one (counting the lengthened ברכה)

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
What is 'seventh'?
Seventh for the long one.
phrases.notes: He means seventh when you also count the regular ברכה that gets stretched out, which the next step names.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 7.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Seventh' means a seventh new ברכה, so there are seven additions.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Seventh' counts the lengthened regular ברכה, so there are only six new ones.
steps.confusionAlert: 'Seventh' here does not mean seven new ברכות. One of the seven is an ordinary daily ברכה that is just made longer.

steps.title: The ברייתא about lengthening גואל ישראל
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that on a fast day the חזן lengthens ברכת גואל ישראל and ends it with a special prayer, followed by שופר blasts.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: in 'Redeemer of Israel' he lengthens, and at its end he says: 'He Who answered אברהם on הר המוריה, He will answer you and hear the sound of your cry this day. Blessed is the Redeemer of Israel.' They answer 'אמן' after him, and the shul's attendant says to them: 'Blow, sons of אהרן, blow!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to support רב נחמן בר יצחק: there really is a regular ברכה that becomes long on a fast day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lengthened ברכה is גואל ישראל, a regular ברכה of שמונה עשרה. It gets a special ending about ה׳ answering אברהם at the עקדה. This proves there is a 'long one' that is counted in the series, while only six ברכות are new.

keyTerms.meaning: As a ברייתא teaches
Redeemer of Israel (a regular ברכה of שמונה עשרה)
He lengthens
Its closing line
The attendant (שמש) of the shul
Blow (the שופר or trumpets)

phrases.english: As a ברייתא teaches:
In 'Redeemer of Israel' he lengthens,
and at its ending he says:
'He Who answered Avraham on Mount Moriah,
He will answer you
and hear the sound of your cry on this day.
Blessed is the Redeemer of Israel.'
And they answer 'Amen' after him,
and the attendant of the shul says to them:
'Blow, sons of Aharon, blow!'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of step 8 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: רב נחמן בר יצחק's claim that one regular ברכה is lengthened and counted in the series
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא describing the lengthening of גואל ישראל on a fast day
steps.whatToRemember: On a fast day גואל ישראל is lengthened and ends with 'He Who answered אברהם on Mount Moriah.' Counting it, the last added ברכה is 'seventh', but only six are new, so the total is 24.

steps.title: The first added blessing and the pattern of blasts
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. The חזן says the next ברכה, ending 'זוכר הנשכחות'. The people answer אמן, and the attendant calls for a תרועה. Every added ברכה follows this pattern, switching between תקיעה and תרועה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then he says the next blessing: 'He Who answered our fathers at ים סוף will answer you and hear your cry today. Blessed... Who remembers the forgotten.' Everyone answers 'אמן,' and the attendant calls out: 'Sons of אהרן, sound a תרועה!' Every blessing works this way. After one he calls 'Blow a תקיעה,' and after the next he calls 'Sound a תרועה.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is still quoting the ברייתא from the last step. It now describes the first added ברכה, the second in the series after the lengthened גואל ישראל, and the pattern that repeats after every one of the added ברכות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each added ברכה mentions a past rescue, here the crossing at ים סוף, and asks ה׳ to answer us the same way today. The people answer אמן, and then the שופר is blown. The calls switch back and forth: one ברכה gets a תקיעה, the next gets a תרועה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Who remembers the forgotten': the closing words of this ברכה
Here this means the synagogue attendant, who calls out instructions. It is not the one leading the prayers.
'Blow!': a call for a תקיעה, one long, steady blast
'Sound a teruah!': a call for a תרועה, a broken, wavering blast
The people's short answer after hearing a ברכה

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two people. The one saying the ברכות is the prayer leader. The חזן הכנסת in this ברייתא is a different person, the attendant who calls for the blasts.

phrases.english: And he goes back and says [the next blessing]:

phrases.aramaic: ״מִי שֶׁעָנָה אֶת אֲבוֹתֵינוּ עַל יַם סוּף,
phrases.english: "He Who answered our fathers at the Red Sea,
He will answer you
and hear the sound of your cry this day.
Blessed [are You, ה׳], Who remembers the forgotten."
And they answer after him, "Amen."
And the synagogue attendant says to them:
"Sound a teruah, sons of Aharon, sound a teruah!"
And so too with each and every blessing:
after one he says, "Blow a tekiah,"
and after the next he says, "Sound a teruah."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא, moving from the first lengthened ברכה to the next one and the repeating pattern.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After each added ברכה the people answer אמן, and the attendant calls for a תקיעה or a תרועה, switching each time.

steps.title: This order is only outside the Temple
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא limits what it just said. This order is only for the גבולין, the places outside the מקדש. In the מקדש it is different, because people do not answer אמן there.
steps.simpleTranslation: When does this apply? Outside the Temple. In the Temple it is not done this way, because people do not answer 'Amen' in the Temple.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא tells us that the order it just described does not apply everywhere. It sets up a separate rule for the מקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'במה דברים אמורים' means 'when does this apply?' It narrows an earlier rule. The difference here is the people's answer: outside they say אמן, but in the מקדש a short אמן is not used.

keyTerms.meaning: 'When is this said?': a phrase that limits an earlier rule
Everywhere outside the מקדש
The Holy Temple

phrases.english: When is this said?
Outside the Temple.
But in the Temple it is not so,
because they do not answer "Amen" in the Temple.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the order from step 10 to places outside the מקדש.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The אמן-and-blasts order is for the גבולין only. In the מקדש people do not answer אמן.

steps.title: What is the source for no Amen in the Temple?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks where we learn that אמן is not answered in the מקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we know that people do not answer 'Amen' in the Temple?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks for a source for the rule it just gave. This sets up the next step, which brings a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא does not just state the rule. It wants to show where the rule comes from in the תנ״ך. The word 'ומנין' always asks for a source.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And from where?': asking for the source of a rule

phrases.english: And from where do we know that they do not answer "Amen"
in the Temple?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the rule given in step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A פסוק that shows אמן is not answered in the מקדש.

steps.title: Every blessing gets its own praise
steps.stepSummary: The answer comes from a פסוק in נחמיה: 'raised above every ברכה and praise.' Someone might think one short answer, like אמן, is enough for every ברכה. The פסוק teaches that each ברכה should get its own full praise.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'Stand up and bless ה׳ your God, from forever to forever, and let them bless Your glorious name, which is raised above every blessing and praise.' You might think one praise is enough for all the blessings. So the verse says 'above every blessing and praise,' meaning that for every blessing you give Him a praise.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its own question by quoting a פסוק and explaining one phrase in it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea being rejected is that all ברכות get the same single short answer, which is אמן. The words 'על כל ברכה' are read as 'for each ברכה, a praise.' So in the מקדש every ברכה gets a fuller praise of its own, not just אמן.

keyTerms.meaning: 'You might think': introduces an idea the ברייתא will reject
'The verse teaches': brings words from the פסוק to correct that idea
Praise

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why the מקדש uses a longer answer instead of אמן. The next steps show what that answer is.

phrases.english: As it says: "Stand up and bless ה׳ your God
from forever to forever,
and let them bless Your glorious name,
which is raised above every blessing and praise."
You might think that for all the blessings together
there should be only one praise.
phrases.notes: He means one short answer, like אמן, said the same way after every ברכה.

phrases.english: So the verse teaches:
"raised above every blessing and praise."

phrases.aramaic: עַל כׇּל בְּרָכָה תֵּן לוֹ תְּהִלָּה.
phrases.english: For every blessing, give Him a praise.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר קוּמוּ בָּרְכוּ אֶת ה׳ אֱלֹהֵיכֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 12 with a פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: נחמיה 9:5, 'raised above every ברכה and praise,' teaches that each ברכה gets its own praise, so a single repeated אמן is not used in the מקדש.

steps.title: So what is said in the Temple?
steps.stepSummary: If אמן is not answered in the מקדש, what does the order there look like?
steps.simpleTranslation: But then, in the Temple, what does he say?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks what the מקדש order is, since it is not the one used outside. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא has only said what is not done in the מקדש. Now it asks for the actual wording used there.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What does he say?'

phrases.english: But then, in the Temple, what does he say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that we know אמן is not used in the מקדש, asks what is said there instead.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact wording of the ברכה, the people's answer, and the call for blasts in the מקדש.

steps.title: The longer Temple ending and response
steps.stepSummary: In the מקדש the ברכה has a longer ending: 'ברוך ה׳ אלהי ישראל מן העולם ועד העולם, ברוך גואל ישראל.' The people answer 'ברוך שם כבוד מלכותו לעולם ועד' instead of אמן. The attendant calls to the כהנים to blow.
steps.simpleTranslation: He says: 'Blessed is ה׳, God of Israel, from forever until forever. Blessed... Redeemer of Israel.' The people answer: 'Blessed is the name of His glorious kingdom forever and ever.' And the attendant calls out: 'כהנים, sons of אהרן, blow!'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its question and gives the full order used in the מקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two changes. The ending of the ברכה gets longer, adding 'מן העולם ועד העולם', which matches the פסוק. The people's answer becomes 'ברוך שם כבוד מלכותו לעולם ועד' instead of אמן. This is the separate full praise for each ברכה that the פסוק required.

keyTerms.term: בָּרוּךְ שֵׁם כְּבוֹד מַלְכוּתוֹ לְעוֹלָם וָעֶד
keyTerms.meaning: The people's answer in the מקדש, said instead of אמן
'Redeemer of Israel': the ending of this ברכה
The כהנים, the sons of אהרן, who blow in the מקדש

steps.whatToRemember: Outside the מקדש, people answer אמן after each fast-day ברכה. In the מקדש, the ending is longer and the people answer 'ברוך שם כבוד מלכותו לעולם ועד', because each ברכה deserves its own full praise.

phrases.english: "Blessed is ה׳, God of Israel,
from forever until forever.
Blessed [are You, ה׳], Redeemer of Israel."
And they answer after him:
"Blessed is the name of His glorious kingdom forever and ever."
phrases.notes: This is what they say in place of אמן.

phrases.english: And the attendant says to them:
"Blow, Kohanim, sons of Aharon, blow!"

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּרוּךְ ה׳ אֱלֹהֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל מִן הָעוֹלָם וְעַד הָעוֹלָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 14 by giving the מקדש wording, which carries out the rule learned from the פסוק in step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: In the מקדש: a longer ending, 'ברוך ה׳ אלהי ישראל מן העולם ועד העולם, ברוך גואל ישראל'. The people answer 'ברוך שם כבוד מלכותו לעולם ועד', and the attendant tells the כהנים to blow.

steps.title: The first added blessing and its response
steps.stepSummary: The prayer leader says the first added ברכה, which ends 'זוכר הנשכחות.' The people answer 'ברוך שם כבוד מלכותו לעולם ועד,' and the חזן הכנסת tells the כהנים to sound a תרועה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then he goes on and says: 'He Who answered אברהם on הר המוריה will answer you and hear your cry today. Blessed is ה׳, God of Israel, Who remembers forgotten things.' The people answer 'Blessed is the name of His glorious kingdom forever.' The חזן הכנסת says: 'Sound a תרועה, כהנים, sons of אהרן!'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא moves on to the first added ברכה, the second in the series after the lengthened גואל ישראל, and describes what happens after it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pattern is the same as for the first ברכה: the people again answer 'ברוך שם' instead of אמן. Two things change. The ברכה now ends 'זוכר הנשכחות' instead of 'גואל ישראל', and the call switches from 'תקעו' to 'הריעו.'

keyTerms.meaning: The mountain where ה׳ answered אַבְרָהָם
'Who remembers forgotten things,' the ending of this ברכה
The attendant who runs the service
'Sound a תְּרוּעָה,' a broken, wavering blast

phrases.english: And he goes on again and says:
"He Who answered Abraham on Mount Moriah,
He will answer you
and hear the sound of your cry on this day.

phrases.aramaic: בָּרוּךְ ה׳ אֱלֹהֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל זוֹכֵר הַנִּשְׁכָּחוֹת״,
phrases.english: Blessed is the Lord, God of Israel, Who remembers the forgotten things."
And they answer after him:
"Blessed is the name of His glorious kingdom forever and ever,"
and the synagogue attendant says to them:
"Sound a teruah, priests, sons of Aaron, sound a teruah, etc."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the order described in step 15 with the first added ברכה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After the second ברכה the people answer 'ברוך שם,' and the call is 'הריעו.'

steps.title: Blasts alternate for every blessing
steps.stepSummary: The same pattern repeats for every extra ברכה. The call switches back and forth between תקיעה and תרועה until all the ברכות are done.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works this way for every ברכה. After one he says 'Blow a תקיעה,' after the next 'Sound a תרועה,' until he finishes them all.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a general rule for all the remaining ברכות so it does not have to spell out each one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 15 and 16 showed the first two ברכות: first תקעו, then הריעו. This line tells us the pattern simply keeps alternating to the end.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Blow a תְּקִיעָה,' a long straight blast
Until he finishes

phrases.english: And so too with each and every blessing:
after one he says "Blow a tekiah,"
and after the next he says "Sound a teruah,"
until he finishes all of them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the first two examples into a general rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תקיעה and תרועה alternate after each ברכה until the end.

steps.title: Two Sages set up this practice in their towns
steps.stepSummary: רבי חלפתא in ציפורי and רבי חנניה בן תרדיון in סיכני followed this order, with 'ברוך שם' and the calls to the כהנים, in their own towns.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is the custom רבי חלפתא set up in ציפורי, and רבי חנניה בן תרדיון in סיכני.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells us that two Sages actually used this order in their cities. This sets up the חכמים' reaction in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both towns were outside the מקדש. That is the key detail, because the next step asks whether this order belongs outside the מקדש at all.

keyTerms.meaning: He set up as a custom

phrases.english: And this is the custom Rabbi Ḥalafta set up in Tzippori,
and Rabbi Ḥananya ben Teradyon in Sikhni.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reports a real-life use of the order just described.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two Sages used this מקדש-style order in towns outside the מקדש.

steps.title: The Sages limit this practice to the Temple
steps.stepSummary: When the חכמים heard about it, they said this order was only done at the eastern gates and on הר הבית, not in other towns.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the matter came before the חכמים, they said: this custom was only done at the eastern gates and on הר הבית.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים react to the custom of ציפורי and סיכני and say it does not belong outside the מקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The order with 'ברוך שם' instead of אמן is a מקדש practice. Copying it in a regular town was not correct.

keyTerms.meaning: The eastern gates of the מִקְדָּשׁ area
The Temple Mount
They only practiced this in

steps.whatToRemember: The order with 'ברוך שם' and the calls to the כהנים belongs to the מקדש. Outside it, the חכמים did not accept it.

phrases.english: And when the matter came before the Sages, they said:
They did not practice this way
except at the eastern gates and on the Temple Mount.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects using the step 18 custom outside the מקדש.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: This order belongs only to the מקדש: the eastern gates and הר הבית.

steps.title: A second version: twenty-four blessings
steps.stepSummary: Some say the practice followed a different ברייתא. In that version the leader says 24 ברכות: the regular שמונה עשרה plus six more.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say it was like this ברייתא: he says 24 ברכות in front of them, the 18 of every day plus six more.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a second version of how the תענית prayer worked, quoting another ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This version starts from the number of ברכות. The next steps will place the extra six and show how the answer differs inside and outside the מקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: And some say (another version)
As was taught in a בָּרַיְיתָא
The 18 ברכות of the daily עֲמִידָה

steps.confusionAlert: Some of the coming lines will look like a repeat of what was said before. This is a separate ברייתא brought as a second version, so the גמרא is quoting it again on purpose.

phrases.english: And some say: as it was taught in a baraita:
He says twenty-four blessings before them:
the eighteen of every day,
and he adds six more to them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another version of what the practice was.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On a תענית the leader says 24 ברכות: 18 plus 6.

steps.title: Where do the six extra blessings go?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks where in the prayer the six extra ברכות are inserted.
steps.simpleTranslation: And those six, where does he say them?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks a simple placement question. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Knowing that six are added is not enough. We also need to know where in the שמונה עשרה they go.

keyTerms.meaning: Where?

phrases.english: And those six, where does he say them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for details about the six added in step 20.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Where the six extra ברכות are placed in the prayer.

steps.title: Between Redeemer and Healer; Amen outside the Temple
steps.stepSummary: The six go between 'גואל ישראל' and 'רופא חולי.' The leader lengthens the גאולה ברכה, and the people answer אמן after each ברכה. That was the practice in the גבולין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Between 'גואל' and 'רופא חולי.' He makes the גאולה ברכה longer, and they answer אמן after every ברכה. This was the practice in the גבולין.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers where the six go and how the people respond outside the מקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Outside the מקדש, the normal response of אמן is used. This is the opposite of the 'ברוך שם' order the חכמים limited to the מקדש in step 19.

keyTerms.meaning: The ברכה ending 'Redeemer of Israel'
The ברכה for healing the sick
Makes it longer
Places outside the מִקְדָּשׁ

phrases.english: Between "Redeemer" and "Healer of the sick,"
and he lengthens the blessing of redemption,
and they answer "Amen" after him
for each and every blessing.
And this was the practice in the outlying places.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The six go between גואל and רופא חולי, and in the גבולין the people answer אמן after each.

steps.title: In the Temple: longer ending, no Amen
steps.stepSummary: In the מקדש the ברכה ends with a long praise and 'ברוך גואל ישראל,' and the people do not answer אמן.
steps.simpleTranslation: But in the מקדש they said: 'Blessed is ה׳, God of Israel, from forever to forever. Blessed is the Redeemer of Israel.' And they did not answer אמן after him.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא contrasts the מקדש with the גבולין described just before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two things change in the מקדש: the ברכה has a longer ending, and the people do not answer אמן. The next steps explain why.

keyTerms.meaning: From forever to forever
The usual response affirming a ברכה

phrases.english: But in the Temple they would say:
"Blessed is the Lord, God of Israel,
from everlasting to everlasting.
Blessed is the Redeemer of Israel."
And they would not answer "Amen" after him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets the מקדש practice against the גבולין practice of step 22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the מקדש there is a longer ending and no אמן.

steps.title: Why such a big difference?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks why the מקדש practice is so different.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why all this?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks for the reason behind the different מקדש practice. This sets up the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question covers both changes: the longer ending and leaving out אמן.

keyTerms.meaning: And why all this?

phrases.english: And why all this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks the reason for step 23.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason the מקדש practice differs.

steps.title: Because Amen is not answered in the Temple
steps.stepSummary: The reason is that אמן is not answered in the מקדש at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because people do not answer אמן in the מקדש.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers with a general rule about the מקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The difference is not special to a תענית. It comes from a broader rule that אמן is never the response in the מקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: Because

phrases.english: Because one does not answer "Amen" in the Temple.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אמן is not answered in the מקדש.

steps.title: Source for no Amen in the Temple
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks how we know that אמן is not answered in the מקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how do we know that אמן is not answered in the מקדש?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks for a source for the rule it just gave. This sets up the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now that the rule is stated, the ברייתא wants a basis for it in a פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: And from where do we know?

phrases.english: And from where do we know that one does not answer "Amen" in the Temple?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of step 25's rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A פסוק showing that אמן is not answered in the מקדש.

steps.title: Each blessing gets its own praise
steps.stepSummary: The source is the פסוק in נחמיה: 'exalted above every ברכה and praise.' This teaches that each ברכה gets its own full praise, not a short אמן.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'Stand and bless ה׳ your God from forever to forever, and let them bless Your glorious Name, which is exalted above every ברכה and praise.' This means: for every ברכה, give Him a praise.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא brings the פסוק from נחמיה and reads it to explain why the מקדש uses a full praise instead of אמן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'above every ברכה and praise' are read as 'for every ברכה, a praise.' In the מקדש each ברכה gets its own full response like 'ברוך שם,' so a short אמן is not used.

keyTerms.meaning: As it says (introducing a פסוק)
And exalted
Praise

steps.whatToRemember: Outside the מקדש the people answer אמן after each ברכה. In the מקדש they answer with a full praise like 'ברוך שם,' because 'for every ברכה, give Him a praise.'
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why the חכמים in step 19 kept the 'ברוך שם' order inside the מקדש only.

phrases.english: As it is said: "Stand up, bless the Lord your God
from everlasting to everlasting,
and let them bless Your glorious Name,
which is exalted above every blessing and praise."

phrases.aramaic: — עַל כׇּל בְּרָכָה וּבְרָכָה תֵּן לוֹ תְּהִלָּה.
phrases.english: For each and every blessing, give Him a praise.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: קוּמוּ בָּרְכוּ אֶת ה׳ אֱלֹהֵיכֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 26 with a פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: נחמיה 9:5 teaches that each ברכה gets its own praise, so a short אמן is not used in the מקדש.

steps.title: The first blessing and its trumpet blasts
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains the order after the first blessing, the lengthened גואל ישראל: a long praise, the people's response, a call to the כהנים, a short prayer, and then the blasts.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: After the first blessing the leader says, 'Blessed is ה׳, God of Israel, from forever to forever. Blessed is the Redeemer of Israel.' The people answer, 'Blessed is the name of His glorious kingdom forever and ever.' The attendant calls, 'Blow, כהנים, blow!' The leader then says, 'The One who answered אברהם on Mount Moriah will answer you and hear your cry today.' Then they blow a תקיעה, a תרועה, and a תקיעה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that spells out step by step what happened after the first blessing of the fast-day prayers in the מקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This fills in the details of what we saw in the previous steps. The long ending replaces a short 'ברוך אתה ה',' and the people answer 'ברוך שם כבוד מלכותו' in place of אמן. Then the חזן הכנסת calls the כהנים to sound the trumpets.

keyTerms.term: בָּרוּךְ שֵׁם כְּבוֹד מַלְכוּתוֹ לְעוֹלָם וָעֶד
keyTerms.meaning: 'Blessed is the name of His glorious kingdom forever and ever.' The response used in the מקדש.
The attendant who directed the order of the service.
They sound a תקיעה, a long straight blast.
They sound a תרועה, a broken or wavering blast.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
On the first one, he says:
phrases.notes: He means the first blessing in the series, the lengthened גואל ישראל, which is not one of the six added on a fast day.

phrases.english: "Blessed is ה׳, God of Israel,
from forever to forever.
Blessed is the Redeemer of Israel."
And they answer after him:
"Blessed is the name of His glorious kingdom forever and ever."
And the attendant says:
"Blow, כהנים, blow!"
And he goes back and says:
"The One who answered Avraham on Mount Moriah,
He will answer you
and hear the sound of your cry this day,"
and they sound a תקיעה, a תרועה, and a תקיעה.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: עַל הָרִאשׁוֹנוֹת הוּא אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the full procedure of the מקדש practice whose source was just explained
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After the first blessing: a long praise, the response 'ברוך שם כבוד מלכותו,' a call of 'תקעו,' the 'מי שענה את אברהם' prayer, then תקיעה-תרועה-תקיעה.

steps.title: The second blessing, and alternating for the rest
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues with the second blessing, which uses 'הריעו' and mentions the Red Sea, and says the calls alternate until all the blessings are done.
steps.simpleTranslation: After the second blessing he says, 'Blessed is ה׳, God of Israel, from forever to forever. Blessed is the One who remembers what is forgotten.' The people answer 'ברוך שם כבוד מלכותו לעולם ועד.' The attendant calls, 'Sound the תרועה, sons of אהרן!' The leader says, 'The One who answered our fathers at ים סוף will answer you and hear your cry today.' They sound a תרועה, a תקיעה, and a תרועה. The same is done for every blessing: one time he says 'תקעו,' the next time 'הריעו,' until all the blessings are finished.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא repeats the same pattern for the second blessing, with a new ending and a new call. Then it tells us to keep alternating for all the remaining blessings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two things change from the first blessing. The call switches from 'תקעו' to 'הריעו,' and the short prayer mentions a different rescue, the Red Sea. The final line sets a rule: the calls alternate for each blessing to the end.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The One who remembers what is forgotten.' The ending of the second blessing.
'Sons of אהרן,' meaning the כהנים.
The Red Sea.
Each and every blessing.

phrases.english: And on the second one, he says:
"Blessed is ה׳, God of Israel,
from forever to forever.
Blessed is the One who remembers what is forgotten."
And they answer after him:
"Blessed is the name of His glorious kingdom forever and ever."
And the attendant says:
"Sound the תרועה, sons of Aharon, sound the תרועה!"

phrases.aramaic: וְאוֹמֵר: ״מִי שֶׁעָנָה אֶת אֲבוֹתֵינוּ עַל יַם סוּף,
phrases.english: And he says: "The One who answered our fathers at the Red Sea,
He will answer you
and hear the sound of your cry this day,"
and they sound a תרועה, a תקיעה, and a תרועה.
And so it is for each and every blessing.
On one, he says "Blow,"
and on the next, he says "Sound the תרועה,"
until he finishes all the blessings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with the second blessing and sets the alternating pattern
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The calls of 'תקעו' and 'הריעו' alternate from blessing to blessing until all are finished.
steps.whatToRemember: Every extra blessing gets a long praise, the response 'ברוך שם כבוד מלכותו,' and trumpet blasts. The calls switch back and forth between 'תקעו' and 'הריעו.'

steps.title: Two רבנים set up this custom in their towns
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא reports that רבי חלפתא in ציפורי and רבי חנניה בן תרדיון in סיכני ran their fasts this way.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is the custom רבי חלפתא set up in ציפורי, and רבי חנניה בן תרדיון in סיכני.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא tells us that this מקדש-style order was actually used outside the מקדש, in two towns. This sets up the חכמים's reaction in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the practice was described as the way things were done in the מקדש. Here we learn that two leaders brought it to their own towns. That raises a question the next line will answer: is this allowed?

keyTerms.meaning: Set up a custom, made it the practice.
ציפורי, a town in the Galil.
סיכני, another town.

phrases.english: And this is the custom רבי חלפתא set up in ציפורי,
and רבי חנניה בן תרדיון in סיכני.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reports that the procedure just described was used outside the מקדש
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי חלפתא and רבי חנניה בן תרדיון used this order in their towns.

steps.title: The חכמים limit the custom to the מקדש
steps.stepSummary: When the חכמים heard about it, they ruled that this order was only used at the Eastern Gates and on הר הבית.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the matter came before the חכמים, they said: This custom was only followed at the Eastern Gates and on הר הבית.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים react to the towns' custom. They say this order belongs only in the area of the מקדש, not out in the towns.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The long praise and the 'ברוך שם' response belong in the מקדש, where אמן is not answered. Outside the מקדש the practice is different, so the towns should not copy it. The חכמים are not rejecting the fast-day blessings. They are only limiting where this special version is used.

keyTerms.meaning: When the matter came before the חכמים.
The Eastern Gates of the הר הבית.
The Temple Mount.

phrases.english: And when the matter came before the חכמים, they said:
They did not follow this practice
except at the Eastern Gates and on הר הבית.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the towns' custom by limiting it to the מקדש
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: This order, with the long praises, the response of 'ברוך שם,' and the call to the כהנים, belongs only at the Eastern Gates and on הר הבית.
steps.whatToRemember: The special trumpet-and-praise order is a מקדש practice. The חכמים did not want it used in other towns.
steps.whyThisMatters: It explains the משנה's story about רבי חלפתא and רבי חנניה בן תרדיון. It shows why the מקדש style, with no אמן, is not copied elsewhere.

steps.title: The גמרא quotes רבי יהודה from the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to a new line in the משנה: רבי יהודה's view that the leader did not need to say זכרונות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: He did not need to say זכרונות, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new part of the משנה and quotes רבי יהודה's opinion. This sets up the question about his reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, the תנא קמא has the leader add the זכרונות and שופרות sections on a fast day. רבי יהודה disagrees and says these were not needed. The גמרא quotes him so it can explain his reasoning.

keyTerms.meaning: The 'Remembrances' section of פסוקים about ה׳ remembering.
'Etc.' The quote continues in the משנה.

phrases.english: רבי יהודה says:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא הָיָה צָרִיךְ לוֹמַר זִכְרוֹנוֹת כּוּ׳.
phrases.english: He did not need to say זכרונות, and so on.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: לֹא הָיָה צָרִיךְ לוֹמַר זִכְרוֹנוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the ברייתא and opens a new topic from the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה holds that זכרונות and שופרות did not need to be said on a fast day.

steps.title: What is רבי יהודה's reason?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אדא דמן יפו asks why רבי יהודה holds that זכרונות are not needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אדא from יפו said: What is רבי יהודה's reason?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אדא דמן יפו asks why רבי יהודה rules this way. He is about to answer his own question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is about reasoning, not about the rule itself. Why would רבי יהודה leave out sections that the תנא קמא includes?

keyTerms.meaning: 'What is the reason?' A question asking for the logic behind a ruling.

phrases.english: רבי אדא from יפו said:
What is רבי יהודה's reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the opinion just quoted
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבי יהודה holds that זכרונות and שופרות are not said on a fast day

steps.title: זכרונות and שופרות are said only at certain times
steps.stepSummary: רבי אדא begins his answer: זכרונות and שופרות are not said except at specific times. The rest of the sentence continues on the daf.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because זכרונות and שופרות are not said... (the sentence continues).
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אדא starts answering. He explains that these sections are limited to certain occasions, and a fast day is not one of them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His answer treats זכרונות and שופרות as fixed for particular times, not as something added to any prayer. That would explain why רבי יהודה leaves them out on a fast day.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Because.' This introduces the reason.
The שופרות section of פסוקים about the שופר.

phrases.english: because זכרונות and שופרות are not said

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question about רבי יהודה's reason
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: זכרונות and שופרות are limited to specific occasions, so they are not said on a fast day. The full list continues on the daf.
